---
title: "3.11 Miscellaneous & Conclusion"
---

- We can combine multiple approaches we have learned throughout the class for flexible model specifications
  - E.g., Can add polynomial terms (e.g., *age^2^*) to a logit/probit model to allow the curve to change directions in a way other than the normal S-curve
- See [Appendix 3E](appendix-3e-functional-forms.qmd) for several examples and advice for flexible IV functional forms in logit/probit models

## Moving forward

- The binary regression model is a building block for most all categorical models:
  - Ordinal and nominal models are straightforward extensions
  - Zero-inflated count models combine count and binary models
- Many latent variable models (for categorical items and/or categorical latent variables) build directly on binary regression models
